newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine phone firms to apply for higher rates.
newsitem.headline: Philippine phone firms to apply for higher rates.

text.p: Three telephone companies led by Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co (PLDT) said on Monday they would file for rate increases in their basic monthly rates this week.

PLDT would ask for a 120 peso increase, or 48 percent, in its current monthly rate of 250 pesos for residential subscribers, and a 180 peso increase, or 31.25 percent, in its 576 peso basic rate charged from commercial users, a senior official said.
"We're going to file our new rates with the National Telecommunications Commission (NTC)," PLDT senior vice president Antonio Samson told reporters.

Bayan Telecommunications Holdings Corp, a unit of Benpres Holdings Corp, said it would seek a 100 peso, or 35.08 percent, increase on its 285 peso monthly rate for residential users, and a 150 to 200 peso, or 25.64 to 34.18 percent, hike for its commercial subscribers who are paying 585 pesos per month.

Globe Telecom vice president Rodolfo Salalima said the company would request a raise in its 270 peso basic rate for residential sbuscribers of 118 pesos or 44 percent, and a 150 to 198 peso, or 25 to 33 percent, increase in its 600 peso monthly billing for corporate clients.

PLDT's Samson said the rate increase would compensate for an impending cut in international call rates. He added that the new rates would be imposed until the company shifted to a call metering mode which is scheduled to be in place by the end of the year.
Charges will then be based on the duration of calls.
The NTC has said it will hold public hearings before deciding on the petitions. - Manila newsroom 63 2 8418938 Fax 8176267
